title: regional-fairness-allocator-and-staged-response-trimming
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: during cross-region failover and regional congestion events, some tenants experience disproportionate shedding (cold-starty or bursty traffic) while others consume a majority of transient capacity. Current admission controller is stateless and FIFO-ish which leads to tail SLO violations for smaller tenants and unpredictable customer experience. Goal: introduce a Regional Fairness Allocator (RFA) that enforces per-region, per-tenant short-window proportional shares and pair it with a Staged Response Trimming (SRT) pipeline that gracefully degrades outputs (token-budgeted trimming, late-token truncation, and cheap-model fallback) before hard-rejecting requests.

Scope and success criteria:
- Implement RFA in serving traffic path with a lightweight state store (per-region sliding counters, leaky bucket windows) so allocation decisions are local but periodically reconciled to control plane metrics.
- Integrate RFA decisions into admission controller such that requests that exceed short-term share are assigned one of three outcomes: delay (small backoff queue), trimmed response (SRT), or admission refusal with structured error (429 + retry-hint).
- SRT modes: (1) token-trim: drop generation budget and synthesize short summary; (2) model-fallback: route to a lower-cost quantized model for shorter latency; (3) metadata-only: return pre-canned minimal structured response if prompt matches known templates.
- End-to-end tests and canary rollout demonstrating per-tenant fairness improvements and no regression on 99th percentile latency for premium customers.

Design notes / architecture:
- Decision point sits in the per-region edge proxy before batching layer; RFA consults in-memory counters and an optional Redis-backed lease for cross-host reconciliation.
- Each tenant has a configurable short-window share (default 10s sliding window) and a longer allowance burst bucket. Small tenants receive a soft deficit priority so they can use at least X tokens/sec even during congestion (configurable to support low-volume customers).
- SRT implements a pluggable sequence of transformers: token-trimmer -> cheap-model router -> canned-response generator. The pipeline emits a structured response envelope indicating degradation-mode for downstream observability.
- Circuit breaker hooks: if a target fallback model is unhealthy, SRT must skip that step and escalate to next degrade mode; the admission controller must integrate CB state to avoid routing to unhealthy endpoints.
- Persisted counters are approximate (d-left or Count-Min) to bound memory; reconciliation corrects drift but does not block decisions.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Stateful per-tenant counters increase memory and operational complexity; mitigations: sharded approximate counters, TTL eviction, and opt-in for very large tenant sets.
- Prefetch/backoff queues add latency for delayed requests; keep delay budget small (<= 150ms) and only for mid-priority lanes.
- Canned/summarized responses reduce perceived fidelity; must be auditable and surfaced in telemetry so customers can see when quality was degraded.
- Complexity of reconciling fairness across regions during global failover: RFA prioritizes region-local fairness. Global fairness will be handled by control-plane rebalancing (separate ticket).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype RFA counters and simple admission decision in dev cluster behind feature flag (ENG-101011-flag). (owner: Miguel)
2) Implement SRT pipeline with 3 degrade modes and unit tests (owner: ServiceInference team).
3) Integrate circuit-breaker checks and health-aware routing (owner: infra-reliability).
4) Build dashboards: per-tenant shed-rate, degradation-mode breakdown, trimmed-token counts, and SLO regressions. Add alerts for unintended broad degradation.
5) Canary rollout on a small set of non-premium tenants for 48h, evaluate metrics, iterate, then expand regions.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- New SLO slice: tenant-availability-rate-in-congestion (target >= 95% for P2/P3 tenants during 99th percentile regional load events).
- Telemetry: emit tags for degradation_mode, rfa_decision, region, circuit_breaker_state, trimmed_token_count.
- Alerts: >5% traffic in a region hitting hard rejects for >5m, or >2% premium traffic trimmed in 5m window.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before removing feature flag):
- Unit and integration tests for RFA and SRT passing in CI.
- Canary run shows median latency change < +10ms for premium routes and 20% lower hard-rejects for small tenants compared to baseline under induced load.
- Dashboards surface degradation and audits show no unauthorized data exposure in canned responses.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/RFA+and+SRT+Design
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1427
- Load test script and results: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1rfa-load-tests

Dependencies:
- ENG-14567 (reserved) - existing token-bucket eviction policy work (reconcile parameter names and burst semantics)
- ENG-23145 - ephemeral priority bands (coordinate priority lanes)
- ENG-41357 - client-aware-degradation hooks (for templated canned responses)

Release plan:
- runtime-1.22.alpha: feature gated build
- runtime-1.22.beta: canary rollout to non-premium tenants in us-west and eu-central
- runtime-1.22: gradual ramp to other regions with monitoring gates

Customer impact: medium
Security review required: false
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI unit + integration tests green. 2) Canary metrics: premium 99p latency regression < 10ms; small-tenant hard-reject rate down >= 20% vs baseline under load. 3) Dashboards show degradation_mode traces and audits pass.
notes: Implementation should avoid strong cross-region coupling. Keep RFA decisions local and conservative. Use feature flags extensively; default off for enterprise customers until validated. Consider a follow-up ticket to add global control-plane signals for inter-region fairness when control plane capacity can reassign delegations.

2025-01-20 | Design: Small UX note — canned responses must include explicit metadata tag "degraded:true" and a short human-readable message for auditability. See design mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/mockups/rfa-srt

2025-01-28 | Code review (infra-reliability): Avoid synchronous Redis calls on the hot path; use async refresh and local lease. Suggested: implement local counters with occasional async reconciliation. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1427#discussion_r223
2025-02-03 | Load test run: synthetic spike in us-west; small tenants saw 27% fewer hard rejects, but premium 99p increased by 12ms during initial config. Tuning in progress to reduce delay budgets.
2025-02-05 | Miguel: Switching to Count-Min sketch reduced memory by ~60% with acceptable 2% allocation drift. Updating doc and tests. Next: add canary gating rules.
